full_judgment:
Md Imman Ali J : This appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgement and order dated 20-4-2008 passed by the High Court Division in Death Reference No. 85 of 2004 with Criminal Appeal Nos. 2006 of 2004 and 2208 of 2004, Criminal Revision No. 856 of 2004, Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 5069 of 2004 and 14993 of 2005, Jail Appeal Nos. 578 of 2004, 579 of 2004, 580 of 2004 and 581 of 2004. By the impugned judgement, the High Court Division accepted the reference so far as it relates to Dipok Dutta Bhola and rejected the same in respect of the remaining four accused persons, dismissed Jail Appeal No. 578 of 2004, discharged the Rule in Criminal Revision No. 856 of 2004 and Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 5069 of 2004 and disposed of the Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 14993 of 2005 and allowed Jail Appeal Nos. 579, 580, 581 .of 2004 and Criminal Appeal No. 2208 of 2004. 

 2. The prosecution case, in brief, was that on 19-4-2003 at 5-30 pm deceased Sreekanta Rakshit, younger son of the informant Shikha Rakshit and Advocate Mridul Kanti Rakshit, aldng with his friend.Jashim Uddin Jessy went out of their house. But he did not return home. So, his mother contacted Jashim Uddin @ Jessy over telephone and came to know that Sreekanta had got down from his rickshaw in front of Collegiate School at Ice Factory Road. The informant became anxious as Sreekanta did not return home. At midnight she informed the matter to Kotwali Police Station. Early in the morning she informed her elder son Sree Kumar Rakshit in Dhaka over telephone. Her husband, Mridul Kanti Rakshit and her daughter used to live in Dhaka in the house of his elder son Sree Kumar Rakshit. At about 12-30 pm she received ft telephone call, from someone naming himself as Bhola, who informed her that the beheaded dead body of her son Sreekanta was lying in Hathatari Police Station. She contacted Hathazari Police Station over telephone and came to know than the beheaded dead body recovered from Lala Chandra Beel of village Shilorpur, had already been sent to the morgue for post mortem examination. At 2-30 pm her elder son arrived home from Dhaka and went to the morgue with his maternal uncle Shovan. They identified the beheaded dead body as that of the deceased Sreekanta. 

 3. The further prosecution case was that accused Azimuddin Mahmud @ Azam, Abdul Hamid, Han Chowdhury, Jahangir Alam, Paritosh Rakshit, Kazal Rakshit, Aparup Rakshit, Arun Rakshit, Barun Rakshit and others had dispute with the father of the deceased over his dwelling house at 44 Hazari Lane, Chittagong. On 25-12-1998 they forcibly occupied a room of the building. Since then accused Elahijan mother of accused Azimuddin, with her domestic help and maid used to live there. The informant filed a criminal case against those accused persons at Kotwali Police Station. Police guards were posted in the house for the safety and security of the members of the informant's family. Accused ABM Fazle Karim Chowdhury, a Member of Parliament, also had enmity with the father of the deceased. He, with a view to grab the property of the father of the deceased, put pressure on him in different ways so that he would leave the country. On 27-3-2003 at 8-00 pm accused Jahangir Alam, Irfan Chowdhury, Paritosh Rakshit, Kazal Rakshit, Arun Rakshit, Saroj Guha, Abdul Hamid, Barun Rakshit, Amit Rakshit and others assembled in the room of accused Elahijan and conspired to kill the deceased in order to occupy the remaining portion of the house. On 16-4-2003 at 12-30 noon, in the office of accused ABM Fazle Karim Chowdhury at Agrabad Commercial Area, the accused persons conspired to kill the deceased. Accordingly, on the night following 19-4-2003 the accused persons took the deceased to the vacant flat on the ground floor of Building No. 1 of Safi Haji at Purba Madarbari, slaughtered him and dumped his beheaded dead body in Lala Chandra Beel and the severed head in Mahamaya Canal. On the next day, on 20-4-2003 at 9-55 pm the informant lodged First Information Report (FIR) with Double Mooring Police Station, which was recorded as Double Mooring Police Station Case No. 19 dated 20-4-2003. 

 4. During investigation of the case, accused Dipok Dutta Bhola was arrested. As a result of his extra-judicial confession, the severed head of the deceased was recovered. Then accused Dipok Dutta Bhola, Jahangir Alam and Md Mobarak Hossain made confessional statements which were recorded by a Magistrate under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The Investigating Officer after investigation submitted charge sheet No. 201 dated 9-8-2003 under sections 302/120-B/364/201/109/34 of the Penal Code against seventeen accused persons of whom Azimuddin Mahmud, Elahijan and Paritosh Rakhit were absconding. 

 5. The case was ultimately transferred to the Divisional Druto Bichar Tribunal, Chittagong, where it was numbered as Druto Bichar Tribunal Case No. 58 of 2003. Charge was framed under sections 120B/302/201/34 of the Penal Code against the accused persons which was read over and explained to the accused on dock, to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 

 7. The defence case, as it transpires from the trend of cross-examination was that the accused persons were innocent and they had been falsely implicated in the case. 

 13. The State filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 5069 of 2004 for setting aside the order of acquittal of accused ABM Fazle Karim Chowdhury, Elahijan @ Aleya Begum, Aparup Rakshit, Amit Rakshit and Shahabuddin Sabu. 

 14. Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 14993 of 2005 was filed by Tandra Dutta, wife of condemned prisoner Dipok Dutta Bhola, directed against the order dated 21-11-2004 passed by the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Chittagong. 

 15. All the aforesaid Criminal Appeals, Jail Appeals, Criminal Revision and Criminal Miscellaneous Case were heard along with the death reference. By the impugned judgement and order, the High Court Division accepted the reference so far as it relates to condemned-prisoner Dipok Dutta Bhola and rejected the reference relating to the remaining four accused persons, dismissed Jail Appeal No. 578 of 2004 preferred by condemned-prisoner Dipok Dutta Bhola, allowed Jail Appeal Nos. 579, 580 and 581 of 2004 and Criminal Appeal No. 2006 and 2208 of 2004, discharged the Rules issued in Criminal Revision Nos. 856 of 2004 and Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 5069 of 2004 and disposed of the Rule issued in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 14993 of 2005. 

 17. On perusal of the impugned judgement, it appears that the High Court Division has minutely dealt with the evidence of all the witnesses as well as other materials on record, and elaborately discussed the relevant aspects of law involved in the case. 

 1. As urged by Mr Probir Haider, learned Counsel appearing for the condemned prisoner Dipok Dutta Bhola. He contends that the confessional statement of the condemned prisoner is not only exculpatory in nature but also not true or voluntary, which is inadmissible in evidence and thus, the High Court Division erred in law in maintaining the conviction relying upon his confessional statement. The learned counsel further argued that the High Court Division erred in law in believing the prosecution story about the recovery of the mutilated head of the victim as per showing of the condemned prisoner in the absence of any corroborative and reliable evidence on record. The learned counsel further argued that the learned Judges of the High Court Division discriminated in con-sidering the case of the condemned prisoner Dipok Dutta Bhola, inasmuch as the other convicts Azimuddin Mahmud, Kamrul Hasan Titu, Mobarak Hossain and Jahangir Alam, who also made confessional statements stood on the same footing with him, but the High Court Division while disbelieving their confessional statements believed the confessional statement of the petitioner without assigning proper reasons. 

 4. As urged by Mr Md Helaluddin Mollah, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner in Jail Petition No. 17 of 2008 that the case against the petitioner was false and concocted by the police for failure to pay large sum of money as demanded by the police officer and for refusing to compromise the case concerning the murder of his own brother. He submits that the case was not proved beyond reasonable doubt by legal evidence. He submits that the petitioner was not named in the FIR and was not identified by the informant in the dock. He further submits that the conviction of the petitioner was based on his confessional statement which was extorted by police torture and is clearly exculpatory, and, therefore, the High Court Division erred in accepting the Death Reference. He further submits that Article 103 of the Constitution has been amended by Act No. 14 of 2011 whereby it is now provided that if the High Court Division upholds the sentence of death or imposes the sentence of death or life imprisonment upon any accused then the accused shall be entitled to prefer appeal as of right before the Appellate Division. He finally submits that 'since the Constitution has been amended giving a beneficial right to the accused, the same right shall accrue to the petitioner although his appeal before the High Court Division was disposed of by a judgement and order which was passed before the amendment to the Constitution." 

 21. There are two aspects to this case, namely conspiracy to murder and the murder itself. According to the prosecution witnesses, there were two incidents of conspiracy, namely on 27-4-2003 in the room of accused Elahijan, and secondly at the office of. ABM Fazle Karim Chowdhury on 16-4-2003, i.e. three days before the occurrence. This was discussed and finalised on 17-4-2003 in the room of accused Elahijan. 

 23. Criminal appeal No. 64 to 66 of 2009 were filed by the State challenging the acquittal of the following accused persons, namely Azim Uddin Mahmud @ Azam, Kamrul Hasan Titu, Md Mobarak Hossain and Md Jahangir Alam. Mr Biswajit Deb Nath, learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the State-appellant submitted that the charge against all the accused persons having been amply proved by probable and competent witnesses, the High Court Division erred in setting aside the conviction and sentence of all the accused persons except Dipok Dutta Bhola. He submitted that the confessional statements of Dipok Dutta Bhola, Jahangir Alam and Mobarak Hossain were true and voluntary, but the High Court Division erroneously left those out of consideration. He further submitted that the trial Court upon proper assessment of the evidence convicted the accused, but the High Court Division most erroneously acquitted all the accused except Bhola. He submitted that the High Court Division under misconception and wrong appreciation of the evidence held all the confessional statements to be inadmissible upon finding that the all the confessing accused were placed in the custody of a police constable just before recording their statements. He pointed out that the form of the confessional statement of Mubarak shows that he was placed in custody of the Court Peon before his statement was recorded. Therefore, that confession was left out of consideration due to misreading and mis-conception. He further submitted that the confessional statement of Mubarak supports the other evidence connecting the accused with the murder of the victim. 

 24. Mr AKM Faiz, learned advocate appearing for the appellant in Criminal Appeal No. 62 of 2009 submitted that there were two instances of conspiracy highlighted in this case and each was supported by cogent evidence. But the High Court Division erred in not considering the positive evidence of the prosecution witnesses. He pointed out that at the earliest point in time the FIR disclosed the conspiracy hatched by the accused. He submitted that the evidence also disclosed the motive for the murder, inasmuch as it was clear that Azam in collusion with highly placed known and named politicians conspired to grab the property belonging to the victim's father. Accused Azam and his mother were already in occupation of a part of the house and were in an unholy alliance with the other accused to get the victim and his family out of the remaining part of the property. 

 30. With regard to accused Azimuddin Mahmud Azam, the High Court Division observed that his conviction by the trial Court was based mainly on the inadmissible confessional statement of three co-accused along with the circumstantial evidence that he had been absconding all along. Relying upon the decision in the case of Hossain vs State, 37 DLR (AD) 139, that abscondence of an accused cannot be held to be corroboration to the confessional statement of another accused so as to base thereon conviction of the absconding accused, the High Court Division concluded that abscondence of Azimuddin Mahmud alone, does not prove his guilt. The other evidence alluded to by the prosecution against Azimuddin Mahmud was the claim of the informant that he had forcibly occupied a portion of the dwelling house of the father of the deceased and was still occupying the same through his mother accused Elahijan. On the other hand, the High Court Division noted that Azimuddin Mahmud claimed to have purchased that portion of the house from the co-sharers of the victim's father and there was no evidence that he had attempted to evict the victim's family from the remaining part of the homestead. The High Court Division also noted that the suit for restoration of possession of the portion occupied by Azimuddin Mahmud, filed by the father of the deceased, was withdrawn. Consequently, the High Court Division did not find the circumstantial evidence to be sufficient to prove the charge against Azimuddin Mahmud under sections 302/201/34 of the Penal Code. 

 44. Turning to the sentence of the appellant Dipok Dutta Bhola, we may refer to the decision of this Division in the case of Nalu vs State, reported in 32 BLD (AD) 247, where the following circumstances were considered as relevant in determining whether the sentence of death should be commuted: 

 45. In the case of Rokia Begun? alias Rokeya Begum reported in 3 LNJ (Lawyers & Jurists) (AD) (2014) 72, this Division also referred to the case of Hazer Ali Manclal vs State, reported in 37 DLR (AD) 87. In that case the conviction and sentence of death was based on circumstantial evidence. The High Court Division commuted the sentence of death to one of imprisonment for life and this Division upheld the decision of the High Court Division. 

 46. In the facts of the instant case, we note that essentially the recovery of the severed head was as a result of direct evidence of the accused himself inasmuch as, in his extra judicial confession he disclosed the location of the severed head of the victim and it was accordingly found at that place in his presence. However, the fact of killing the victim prior to disposal of the dead body and the severed head was supported only by circumstantial evidence and the confession of co-accused Mobarak. As we have stated earlier the confession of accused Dipok Dutta Bhola was rightly left out of consideration by the High Court Division. There is no direct evidence with regard to the assault on the victim which resulted in his death. 

 48. In the case of Rokia Begum alias Rokeya Begum reported in 3 LNJ (Lawyers & Jurists) (AD) (2014) 72, this Division referred to the case of Nowsher Ali vs State, reported in 39 DLR 57, which is a decision of the High Court Division. and the subsequent observation of this Division when that case was brought before it, to the effect that "In some cases inordinate delay in execution of death sentence may be considered a ground for commuting it to transportation for life " In that case of Nowsher Ali vs Stale, the High Court Division had considered that a delay of 6 years may be considered for commutation of death sentence to life imprisonment. In the instant case the condemned prisoner has suffered in the condemned cell for over 10 years and 8 months and thus the length of period can be taken as one of the reasons to commute the sentence of death to one of imprisonment for life.
